title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Liverpool: Familiar Villain Ends Blues’ Carabao Cup Dreams
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:57 PM EDTWesley Fofana (middle) missed the decisive kick in the penalty shootout. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesChelsea are out of Carabao Cup competition in round four, after losing to Liverpool 6–5 on penalties following a 1–1 draw at regular time at Anfield on Wednesday night.
The hosts looked slightly better from the start, but it was a vastly uneventful opening half, with both teams struggling to get much of anything going offensively.

That all changed in the final 10 minutes of the first half, thanks to some woeful defensive mistakes. Ryan Gravenberch brought down Moisés Caicedo inside the penalty area with a clumsy, unnecessary challenge. Morgan Rogers then converted from the spot to give Chelsea the lead 40 minutes in with the very first shot on goal from either team.

Chelsea’s joy was short-lived, though, as Wesley Fofana inexplicably put his hand up defending a corner, resulting in an egregious handball. Cody Gakpo capitalized on Fofana’s gift and equalized from the spot to send the game level into the break.

The second half was much more open, and both teams had clear chances that required the pair of goalkeepers to make crucial saves. Still, neither side could find a winner, and the game was decided in a penalty shootout.

The shootout went to sudden death after Chelsea’s Valentín Barco and Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas missed inside the opening five penalties taken. Chelsea had a chance to complete the upset, but Emmanuel Emegha missed what would’ve been the winning penalty—and it proved costly.
Needing to score to extend the shootout, Fofana sent his penalty into orbit to tie the bow on his nightmare of a game.

For the third time since 2019, Chelsea’s Carabao Cup dreams ended in a penalty shootout against Liverpool. Now, Xabi Alonso’s men have only the Premier League and the FA Cup to fight for in what remains of 2026–27.

Estévão was an unused substitute against Liverpool.  / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesIt’s been only a year since an 18-year-old Estêvão scored a match-winner against Liverpool and then proceeded to steal the show with a dazzling performance against Barcelona in the Champions League. The Brazilian appeared destined to continue growing in importance for Chelsea in the coming months. That couldn’t be further from what actually happened.

Four days after Alonso picked fellow teenager Geovany Quenda ahead of him to replace João Pedro in the XI against Tottenham, Estévão was again omitted from the lineup against Liverpool—the first time he didn’t feature from the start in the Carabao Cup this season. Although first-choice attackers Pedro and Cole Palmer were unavailable, the Brazilian didn’t even feature from the bench.

Estévão hasn’t started for Chelsea since Sept. 9, and has played just 31 minutes in four appearances for the Blues since. In total, the Brazilian attacker has played 172 minutes for the Blues through 11 games across all competitions this term.

Last summer, Estévão was considered a superstar in the making and a potential future Ballon d’Or winner. He’s already shown he has the raw quality to blossom into a star, but he currently finds himself way down Alonso’s attacking pecking order.

Only Alonso knows the reasons why Estévão is barely getting opportunities, but it’s undeniable that the development of one of the most exciting young prospects in the sport is getting compromised. Alonso’s treatment of Estévão is starting to look eerily similar to how Carlo Ancelotti treated Endrick at both Real Madrid and Brazil.
If the situation doesn’t improve, then the noise surrounding his potential Chelsea exit in coming transfer windows—presumably on loan—will only intensify.
Morgan Rogers continued his incredibly productive start of the season.  / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Mike Penders—7.8: Nervous on the ball, often lobbing the ball high up the pitch instead of playing an easy pass, leading to frustration from teammates. Still, he produced a couple of brilliant saves in the second half.

RB: Josh Acheampong—7.5: Had a tasty battle down the flank with Rio Ngumoha and more held his own. He also occasionally ventured forward and caught Liverpool by surprise with a couple of nice runs to the byline. Stunning block late to deny Bradley Barcola.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—6.6:  Was vigilant and diligent in his defensive duties until he was forced to exit the pitch injured on the brink of half time.
CB: Wesley Fofana—7.6: Cost his team by gifting away a penalty immediately after taking the lead and then missed the decisive penalty in the shootout. A nightmare evening for the Frenchman.
